title: Codex subagent handoff remains traceable
description: Acceptance scenario for a Codex app-server parent run that delegates to a child agent and preserves machine-checkable parent/child run evidence.

platform.rationale: Codex subagent handoffs need child-run evidence before Platform can score delegated work without scraping logs.

assumptions.workflow: Parent Codex thread spawns a child agent, waits for it, observes completion, and finalizes with parent-run evidence.
assumptions.correctnessModel: A successful handoff records spawn and wait provider tools, child-run start/completion, and parent/child agent-run anchors.
assumptions.threatModel: Delegated work must not disappear into provider-only logs or lose correlation to the parent agent run.
researchBasis: Long-horizon agent evals need child-run semantics as first-class evidence.
Subagent delegation should be scored from stable run IDs, not human-readable transcripts.
Trace join keys are required before multi-agent trajectories can be promoted into shared Platform storage.
